gaps: NO ERROR BOUNDARY ANYWHERE (verified: grep for componentDidCatch/ErrorBoundary/getDerivedStateFromError across src/ returns zero hits). The Shop is a 1149-line component mounted simultaneously with every other section on page load. A single render throw in the Shop subtree (now or introduced by the heavy Phase 3-5 feature work the plan adds) takes down the ENTIRE portfolio for every visitor, including those who never scroll to the game. The plan adds vitest but no React error boundary around the Shop section. This is the single cheapest, highest-leverage robustness fix the plan omits: wrap the Shop (or each section) in an error boundary so a game crash degrades to a fallback card instead of a white-screened resume.

THE BALANCE-GATE PREMISE IS BUILT ON A FILE THAT DOES NOT EXIST. The plan's risk section and Phase 1/2 repeatedly gate the entire economy rebalance behind 'the deterministic Monte-Carlo balance test' and cite economy-sim.mjs as the source of the 89%/96% win-rate numbers. I verified _audit/ contains only day1-check.mjs, depth-hold.mjs, rapport-softlock.mjs, reveal-schedule.mjs — there is NO economy-sim.mjs. The multiple verifications already caught this ('the finding mis-cites a non-existent economy-sim.mjs'). The plan inherits those headline numbers (~50-70% margin, ~90-96% win) as settled fact and proposes to tune AGAINST them, but the canonical sim was never committed. Before any rebalance, the actual harness must be (re)built and committed as the vitest balance-regression test; otherwise Phase 1 tunes against numbers nobody can reproduce.

RECORDS SCHEMA HAS NO MIGRATION PATH, yet Phase 5 adds achievements, tokens, daily-best, and per-condition lore to it. Verified: loadRecords (Shop.jsx:115-123) only does {...DEFAULT_RECORDS, ...JSON.parse(raw)} against key 'kaitosCurios.records.v1'. New nested fields (e.g. achievements:{}, unlocks:{}) merge shallowly, so a returning visitor with old v1 data gets new top-level keys defaulted but any nested/renamed shape silently breaks. The plan's useRecords refactor (Phase 2) mentions 'add an explicit version/migrate step' only in a low-severity finding; it should be a hard prerequisite BEFORE Phase 5 writes new fields, or early adopters' saved progress corrupts.

THE PLAN NEVER COMMITS TO A SINGLE WIN-RATE FIX SEQUENCE AND UNDER-WEIGHTS ITS OWN STATED RISK. The plan correctly flags that killing the same-day re-flip is 'the riskiest single change ... removes the ONLY currently-viable loop' and that demand-forecast + saturation must ship together. But Phase 1 lists these as six separate bullets with no enforced atomic-merge boundary, and the quickWins/roadmap let a developer ship the rent steepening or re-flip kill independently. For a solo portfolio dev this WILL be done piecemeal. The plan should explicitly mark the Phase-1 economy set as a single non-divisible PR gated on the (rebuilt) balance sim, not a checklist.

DEAD/OPT-OUT EDGE: 'Quick deal' relabel + the unwanted opening-offer bump (0.38 -> 0.50) is listed as a quick win, but the plan never reconciles it with the same-day-reflip kill. After Phase 1 suppresses the wanted bonus on same-day-bought items (falling back to dumpFactor 0.62), the sell opening offer math at shopEngine.js:247 (value*0.85 wanted / 0.38 unwanted) interacts with that change — a same-day-bought wanted item will now be priced as unwanted, so the 0.38->0.50 fix and the re-flip kill touch the SAME code path and must be designed together, not as a standalone quick win plus a separate Phase-1 item.

NO ASSET/PORTRAIT LICENSING OR SOURCING NOTE. The story payoff (the entire point) renders Kaito portraits from /Dialog/Pictures/*.webp reused from elsewhere on the site (PORTRAITS map in shopData.js references WaveOpenNeck, ThumbsUp, Embarrassed, etc.). Phase 5 'pair portrait expression swaps with QUIPS' and adds a mood system needing eager/wary/stubborn faces — but the plan never confirms those portrait variants EXIST or who authors them. If the haggle-mood feature needs 3 new expressions per outcome and the art isn't there, that feature silently can't ship. The plan should inventory available portraits before scoping mood-driven expression swaps.
overengineering: TYPESCRIPT CONVERSION (Phase 2) is an L-effort task with marginal payoff for a 533-line pure engine that already has a clean discriminated-by-side haggle object. The verification on the TS finding is 'unverified' and even the finding offers JSDoc+checkJs as an equivalent. For a portfolio whose differentiator is the GAME and the STORY, a full TS migration burns budget that should go to the story-reachability fix and economy rebalance. Cut to: JSDoc @typedef on State/Action/Haggle + checkJs if any typing at all. The vitest reducer tests already catch the 'wrong field on wrong side' class of bug TS would prevent.

THE FULL 'roguelite bones' DIRECTION (meta-currency, between-run caravan upgrade shop, 1-of-3 perk drafting, endless/ascension mode, difficulty modes Cozy/Trader/Cutthroat) is XL scope creep the plan's own risk section warns against, yet Phase 5/6 still enumerate all of it. For a recruiter who plays 5 minutes, NONE of this lands — they win once, see the story, and leave. Cut the meta-currency/upgrade-shop/ascension entirely. Keep ONLY: a graded end-of-run RANK and the fourth-wall close. Perk drafting (1-of-3) is the one depth lever worth keeping IF the perk catalog is expanded, but it's optional, not core.

DAILY/SHAREABLE SEED (Phase 5/6) is a feature for a competitive-roguelike community this game will never have. A portfolio visitor does not return daily to compare seeds. The determinism infra exists, so it's 'cheap', but cheap-and-pointless is still pointless — it's UI surface area and a 'Daily' entry point to maintain for zero recruiter value. Cut it; keep only 'Replay this seed' if anything (useful for a player who lost a close run).

FULL PORTRAIT MOBILE SHOP LAYOUT (Phase 6: stack HUD, move demand board, 2-wide shelf, horizontal bag strip) is L-effort for a desktop-leaning portfolio whose other sections are also landscape-gated. The DIMENSION-AWARE GATE FIX (allow tablet/desktop portrait, friendlier copy) is the real win and is S-effort. Do that; treat the bespoke portrait Shop layout as explicitly out-of-scope, not 'optional polish.' The audit itself rates this lower confidence (0.7) and the engine decoupling doesn't change that the CSS work is large.

THE 40-48 ITEM CATALOG + tripled quip buckets + dealBuy/dealSell split + no-repeat guard + 6-8 mechanically-distinct special items (Phase 5 content breadth) is content-mill work the plan's own risk note flags ('the fourth-wall close + guaranteed story payoff matter far more than a 40-item catalog'). Floor Relic/Food at 3 items each (a handful of SVGs) and STOP. The special-items-with-unique-rules (appreciates-if-held, matched sets, collector-pays-3x) is a whole new mechanic surface that needs its own balance pass — cut it unless the hold-loop from Phase 1 actually lands first.

UNIFIED EVENTS QUEUE replacing sfx.n/toast.n (Phase 2) is a clean refactor but 'unverified' and solves a problem the game doesn't have yet (multiple cues per action). The current two-counter pattern works. Only build the events queue if/when Phase 5's coin-burst + screen-shake juice is actually being implemented — don't refactor the side-effect channel speculatively as foundational work.
missingDimensions: ERROR HANDLING / RESILIENCE: no React error boundary around the Shop or any section (verified absent). Given all sections mount on load and the Shop is the largest/most-complex, an uncaught render error white-screens the whole portfolio. This is a hard prerequisite that the plan, focused on engine purity and tests, never mentions.

PERFORMANCE BUDGET for the always-mounted-offscreen architecture: the plan touches this (defer createRun, content-visibility:auto) but never sets a measurable budget or measures the actual cost. For a portfolio, Lighthouse/TTI on the homepage matters more than any in-game tweak — the heavy Phase 5 visual work (coin bursts, micro-interactions, more items/icons) all loads at page mount for every visitor. A concrete 'homepage TTI must not regress' gate is missing.

ANALYTICS / CONVERSION INSTRUMENTATION: the entire vision is 'a hiring manager plays 5 min and converts to exploring the rest of the site.' There is zero plan to MEASURE that — no event on game-started, story-card-seen, win-reached, fourth-wall-CTA-clicked. Without it, you cannot tell if the showpiece works. For a recruiter-conversion device this is the most important missing dimension; even a single lightweight counter on 'reached the Finofo card' and 'clicked through to Projects' would validate the whole thesis.

SEO/META / SOCIAL PREVIEW: a portfolio's game section is invisible to a link-share or search crawler (it's behind a scroll + a portrait gate + client-side render). No mention of an OG image / meta description that advertises the game, so the 'showpiece' is undiscoverable except by someone already scrolling. Relevant because the whole point is recruiter reach.

REDUCED-DATA / LOW-END DEVICE PATH: the plan adds significant juice (coin bursts, screen shake, more infinite animations, deal-struck moments) but only references prefers-reduced-MOTION. There's no prefers-reduced-data or low-end fallback, and the offscreen infinite animations already burn GPU on every page load. A recruiter on a throttled laptop/phone is a real audience.

additionalFindings.title: No error boundary: a Shop render throw crashes the entire portfolio for all visitors
additionalFindings.recommendation: Wrap each section (or at minimum the Shop) in a React error boundary that renders a graceful fallback. Verified: zero error-boundary implementations exist in src/. Because Home.jsx mounts all sections simultaneously at page load (Home.jsx:180-190) and the Shop is the largest, riskiest subtree (and gets the most new feature code in Phases 3-5), an uncaught error white-screens the whole site even for visitors who never reach section 4. This must land in Phase 0 alongside the story-reachability fix, not be deferred.

additionalFindings.title: The plan's quick-win 'raise unwanted opening offer 0.38->0.50' collides with the Phase-1 same-day-reflip kill at the same code path
additionalFindings.recommendation: shopEngine.js:247 computes the sell opening offer as value*(wanted?0.85:0.38). Phase 1 proposes suppressing the wanted bonus for same-day-bought items (treating them as unwanted -> dumpFactor). After that change, a same-day-bought wanted item routes through the 0.38 branch, so the opening-offer fix and the re-flip kill must be designed as one change. Listing the 0.38->0.50 bump as a standalone quick win risks shipping it before the economy rebalance and then re-touching it — sequence them together or hold the quick win until Phase 1.

additionalFindings.title: ackBackstory unconditionally calls generateDay, so a tier crossed on the FINAL trading night plus the win path can never both resolve
additionalFindings.recommendation: Verified at shopEngine.js:442-462 + 480-488: sleep() returns at the win branch (442) before the tier check (451), and ackBackstory (480) ALWAYS runs generateDay -> phase 'shop'. The plan's Phase-0 fix correctly moves tier-drain above the win check and adds a pendingTiers queue, but must also handle the case where the queue empties on a victory night: ackBackstory needs to route to 'win' (not generateDay->'shop') when day>=victoryDay. The plan mentions this in one item but the engine helper enterShopAfterDayGen() it proposes would wrongly generate a day-9 board on a win. Make the post-queue routing branch on victory explicitly.

additionalFindings.title: Records key is hard-coded 'kaitosCurios.records.v1' with shallow merge only; no forward-migration before Phase 5 expands the schema
additionalFindings.recommendation: loadRecords (Shop.jsx:115-123) does {...DEFAULT_RECORDS, ...stored}. This is safe for adding flat fields but will silently break on any nested/renamed structure (achievements maps, unlock objects, daily-best records) that Phase 5 introduces. Add a versioned migrate(stored) step and bump to .v2 BEFORE writing any new shape, or returning players lose/corrupt progress. Make this a hard gate on the Phase-2 useRecords extraction rather than a low-severity nice-to-have.

additionalFindings.title: The help text actively teaches a strictly-losing line ('Hold the rest ... stash it and wait') in TWO places, and the plan only fixes the mechanic, not both copy sites
additionalFindings.recommendation: Shop.jsx:1033-1035 (help panel) AND the in-haggle sell note both advise holding non-wanted items, which is net-negative under the current economy (verified: dump ceil 0.62x value < buy floor >=1.03x value, and recurrence is ~21-40%/day). Until the Phase-1 demand-forecast + saturation actually make holding +EV, BOTH copy sites must be corrected, not just the help panel. The plan's roadmap references the help line but the duplicate in-haggle note (the live decision point) is the more damaging one and isn't called out.

verdict: PARTIALLY — the plan would reach 'genuinely good portfolio game,' and IF Phases 0-2 are executed faithfully it credibly reaches 'industry-standard ENGINEERING.' But as written it overshoots 'industry-standard GAME' on scope (Phases 3-6 are a commercial-roguelite wishlist the plan's own risks disown) while leaving two real industry-standard PRODUCTION gaps unaddressed: no error boundary (a Shop crash white-screens the whole portfolio) and no analytics to prove the recruiter-conversion thesis the entire vision rests on. The diagnosis is excellent and unusually honest — it correctly converges on the one defect that matters (the story payoff is unreachable for players who win) and correctly identifies the solved economy as the second. The single most important thing to get right is NOT any single code fix: it is to ship the Phase-0 story-reachability fix (move tier-drain above the win check + pendingTiers queue + a 'Hear the rest' button on the win screen) WITH its multi-tier-drain and win-night vitest tests in the SAME commit, AND to rebuild/commit the balance Monte-Carlo harness (the cited economy-sim.mjs does not exist) before touching the economy — because every other theme is downstream of 'the player meets the real Kaito,' and that fix touches the most load-bearing engine path where a silent regression re-hides the entire reason the game exists. Concretely: do Phase 0 + the vitest harness + an error boundary, cherry-pick only the haggle-mood/per-item variety and the graded RANK + fourth-wall close from later phases, add a single conversion event, and explicitly cut TS migration, meta-currency, daily seeds, the full portrait layout, and the 40-item catalog. That is the version that actually feels AAA at portfolio scope without burning the budget on machinery a 5-minute player never sees."}
